A healthcare worker carries an infant infected with the Ebola virus in a treatment centre in Beni, North Kivu Province, Congo, November 9, 2026 [Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP]By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 15 Nov 202615 Nov 2026
Africa’s top public health agency says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is still not under control six months after it was declared.
“If we don’t stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak that the world will have,” Jean Kaseya, director-general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), told Reuters news agency on Sunday.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Anthrax outbreak kills hippos in DR Congo’s Virunga National Parklist 2 of 3Health authorities probe two suspected Ebola cases in northeast Nigerialist 3 of 3Ebola death toll in DR Congo passes 5,000end of list
Since the outbreak was announced on May 15, more than 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths have been recorded, according to government data.
Kaseya said that more than “80 percent of ‌new cases emerge outside contact lists and over 65 percent of deaths” have occurred in the community outside health centres.
Cases have now been reported in East, Central and West Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date.
“We are all in agreement today to say that this outbreak is still serious, and is ⁠still not under control,” Kaseya said.
The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which can trigger haemorrhagic fever.

Britain’s Prince Harry has met wounded veterans and medics in Ukraine during a surprise visit.
The royal family member attended Ukraine’s National Invictus Games and a conference for medics in the western city of Lviv on Saturday. It was organised by Superhumans, a clinic that specialises in the rehabilitation of war-wounded.

“Every single time I come back to Ukraine, I feel welcome, I feel warmth,” Harry said, adding that he’d “taken a risk to come here”.
Ukraine has about 1.4 million combat veterans, more than 10 percent of whom have disabilities.
“You’re going to win the war,” the 42-year-old British royal said during his fourth trip to the country since the start of the conflict with Russia in 2022.Prince Harry at Ukraine’s National Invictus Games in Lviv [Credit: Lviv Oblast Military Administration handout via Al Jazeera]
The prince watched wheelchair rugby players competing for a place in Ukraine’s team for next year’s Invictus Games in Birmingham in England.
Around 500 people have registered to compete to qualify for the 60-member squad – the largest ever team – that Ukraine is planning to send to the 2027 event.
“You’re going to win the war and then you’re going to be set up for success,” he said.

A road leads from Russia into Estonia at the Luhamaa border crossing on October 3 [File: Carl Court/Getty Images]By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 15 Nov 202615 Nov 2026
Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia, after an attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blames on Moscow.
The foreign minister made the announcement on Sunday, after eight people were detained overnight in connection with an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems.

Morocco are the first African and Arab football team to qualify for back-to-back World Cup quarterfinals [File: Bernadett Szabo/Reuters]By Hafsa AdilPublished On 15 Nov 202615 Nov 2026
Morocco have become the first Arab country to enter FIFA’s top five men’s team rankings after moving up by two places from their previous best position of number seven.
The two-time World Cup quarterfinalists leapt ahead of Brazil and Portugal on points on Sunday, following their strong performance in recent continental football matches.
Morocco are also the first African and Arab country to reach back-to-back quarterfinals at the World Cup, where the continent’s top-ranked nation was knocked out by France in consecutive tournaments.
The Atlas Lions’ 2026 finish did not improve or match their semifinal run at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, where they surpassed all expectations to become Africa and the Arab world’s first semifinalists and the darlings of the tournament.
Following the World Cup in North America, Mohamed Ouhabi’s team have maintained a 100 percent record in the current round of qualifying matches for the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) 2027.
Morocco thumped Niger 5-0 in their latest qualification match on Friday, as the star-studded lineup shone in front of a raucous home crowd in Rabat.
AFCON’s defending champions lead Group A by nine points.
However, their AFCON title is contentious and is subject to a hearing at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) following an appeal by losing finalists Senegal.
Senegal were stripped of this year’s AFCON title and Morocco were declared champions by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), despite Senegal beating the hosts ⁠⁠⁠⁠1-0 after extra time in January’s final in Rabat. Advertisement

Smoke following a ballistic missile attack attributed to the Houthis on the outskirts of Aden on Friday [Stringer/Reuters]By Al Jazeera Staff and ReutersPublished On 15 Nov 202615 Nov 2026
Forces affiliated with Yemen’s internationally recognised government say they are withdrawing from territory near the Bab al-Mandeb strait to focus on defending the interim capital, Aden, from the Houthi armed group.
A spokesman for the Southern Armed Forces, a group allied with the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, said on Sunday that it was redeploying from Dhubab airport and areas around Bab al-Mandeb in southwestern Yemen.
Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Fighting intensifies in Yemen as Houthis deny targeting Meccalist 2 of 4Yemen’s Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia as UNSC extends sanctionslist 3 of 4Siege fuels disease fears in Yemen’s Taizlist 4 of 4Saudi-led coalition intercepts suspected Houthi missiles and dronesend of list
“This step is taken based on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats,” the spokesman said.
The announcement raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden on the southern coast, the base of the internationally recognised government since the Houthis drove leaders from the capital Sanaa more than a decade ago.
Reinforcements would also be sent to try to end the Houthis’ siege of Taiz, where fighting has been raging to the west of the city, the announcement added.
Humanitarian conditions are worsening in Yemen’s third-largest city, with aid supplies blocked from entering and civilians unable to leave.
